Update, Eastern Time 10:13 PM: Apple has now confirmed the launch is for customers with Visa and Mastercard credit cards issued by Axis Bank. Original text below.

Almost 12 years after Apple first announced Apple Pay, the feature has finally launched in India today, becoming one of the few major markets without Apple Pay until now. Here are the details.

Apple Pay finally expands to India

As TechCrunch previously reported, Apple Pay will launch in India "later on Tuesday", with Axis Bank as the first partner bank.

Now, as discovered by Aaron Perris on X, Apple has started activating Apple Pay support for India on its servers, meaning the launch is officially underway.

According to Apple's support article, Apple Pay is now supported in 101 countries and regions, including India.

India has quickly become one of Apple's most strategically important countries, both in terms of manufacturing and consumer growth.

Beyond expanding its retail business and repeatedly emphasising strong growth in India during quarterly earnings calls, Apple and its suppliers have also been shifting more iPhone production lines to India as part of a broader strategy to diversify manufacturing away from China.

However, this expansion is not without controversy. Apple is currently defending itself against an antitrust case brought by India's Competition Commission over how the App Store operates, while the company has also refused to comply with a government order requiring smartphone makers to pre-install a state-operated application on new devices.

Apple's manufacturing partner Tata Electronics has also recently come under fire after an Indian pollution regulator alleged that wastewater discharged from one of its iPhone component factories contaminated groundwater and nearby farmland.

Tata has also recently been the target of cyberattacks, with confidential files allegedly belonging to several companies including Apple being leaked as a result.

Despite all of the above, Apple's launch of Apple Pay in India represents another milestone in the company's broader expansion in the country, and may have come at just the right time for its services business.

In the previous fiscal quarter, Apple's services business revenue saw its first quarter-on-quarter decline since Q4 of fiscal year 2022. Of course, the Indian market alone may not turn things around, but with iPhone sales reaching record highs locally, Apple Pay gives the company another way to sustain this growth momentum.
